answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each agent to stake a small deposit of nectar tokens before joining a service island, where the stake is locked for the epoch and forfeited on verified misbehavior, so creating thousands of fake identities costs real capital. Honest agents earn their stake back plus fees, while a ripple of forfeitures punishes anyone flooding the market — each extra identity costs a deposit, so the marginal profit of the next sybil collapses below its price.
